title: Hotfix: align perf-canary p95 aggregation window between runtime and telemetry pipeline
author: Caleb Johnson
description: Context: During perf-canary phase-1 rollout we got a false positive page for a ~12–18% p95 latency “regression” that did not reproduce in runtime logs/traces. Root cause was a mismatch between how the runtime emits the canary p95 signal (pre-aggregated over a 60s sliding window) and how the telemetry pipeline rolls it up (recording rule computed p95 over a 5m range, effectively double-windowing and amplifying low-sample jitter after deploy/warmup). This PR hotfixes the mismatch by switching perf-canary latency reporting to histogram-based aggregation end-to-end and standardizing the quantile computation window at 5 minutes in the telemetry rules (single source of truth). Changes: (1) Runtime: stop emitting pre-aggregated canary p95 gauge; emit latency histogram buckets (+sum/+count) for canary requests tagged source=perf-canary and request_class=canary-safe. (2) Telemetry: update perf-canary recording rules to compute p95 via histogram_quantile over a 5m rate window, consistent with canary detector expectations and dashboards. (3) Guardrails: add a unit test that asserts the 5m window constant in rules and a small ingestion test that ensures the histogram series is present and the legacy gauge is absent. Notes: This is a surgical hotfix intended to eliminate paging noise; follow-up work to update downstream dashboards/alerts in observability-pack is tracked separately (see ENG-2845/ENG-2846).
commits: telemetry: compute perf-canary p95 via histogram_quantile over 5m window
runtime: emit perf-canary request latency histogram (bucket/sum/count) and remove p95 gauge
tests: validate perf-canary quantile window + series shape to prevent regressions
docs: inline comments on window semantics and why gauge is prohibited here
review_conversation: Logan Wright (Telemetry): The root cause description matches what we saw in the backfill graphs. Strong +1 on removing the pre-aggregated p95 gauge; double-windowing is a footgun. Can you confirm the histogram buckets follow our standard boundaries (so dashboards can reuse shared panels)?
Caleb Johnson (author): Yep—using the shared latency bucket set from telemetry/metrics/latency_buckets.h (same as gateway latency). No custom buckets and no window label.

Nadia Rahman (Metrics definitions): Please make sure the recording rule uses [5m] consistently (I saw a leftover [1m] in a comment on the first push). Also, can we keep the metric name stable for the detector? It currently reads ri.perf_canary.latency.p95_ms.

Caleb Johnson (author): Updated: rules now compute p95 into the same recording series name ri.perf_canary.latency.p95_ms, sourced from the histogram. The old gauge series ri.perf_canary.latency.p95_ms_raw is removed (was only used internally and not referenced by detector). Added test to fail if the window is not 5m.

Sean Gallagher (SRE): This should reduce pager fatigue. Two asks: (1) add a deploy-note in the PR so oncall knows why the graph shape changes; (2) confirm no cardinality blow-up from new histogram labels.

Caleb Johnson (author): Added release note snippet below + verified label set stays within the perf-canary allowlist (model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode, le). No request_id, no prompt_hash, no window. Cardinality check passes.

Thomas Baird (Cardinality controls): le label is expected, but please confirm you aren’t adding any “bucket_id”/custom dimension. Also please ensure the old gauge is actually removed (otherwise we carry both).
Caleb Johnson (author): Confirmed: only standard Prometheus histogram le. Gauge emission is fully deleted from runtime. Added ingestion test to assert gauge series is absent.
Allison Grant (Observability standards): Nit: can we add a short comment in rules about why [5m] is the contract window (detector baseline + noise handling)? Avoid future “optimize to 1m” changes.
Caleb Johnson (author): Added comment + linked ENG-2846 in-line. Thanks.

Omar El-Sayed (Runtime instrumentation): Runtime side looks fine. One concern: canary-safe requests can be low volume at off-hours; histogram_quantile can be noisy if there are no samples. Do we have a minimum sample guard upstream?

Caleb Johnson (author): Detector already enforces minimum sample size before paging (ENG-2846). This change should be strictly better than the gauge because we won’t be applying percentile-on-percentile anymore.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Approved once CI is green.

release_notes: Perf canary: standardized p95 latency computation to a single 5m histogram-based rollup to eliminate false positives caused by aggregation-window mismatch (no customer traffic impact; internal signal only).
